trickyParts: The harness for the browser suite is built on the issue volume and survives a pod replacement only as a script: /legion/harness/setup.sh is idempotent (Postgres 17 + pgvector unpacked from Debian packages under /legion/harness/pg, a cluster on 127.0.0.1:55432, one database per role lane, the Playwright browsers under /legion/harness/ms-playwright, GOCACHE and GOMODCACHE beside them) and /legion/harness/env.sh is what every harness command sources. The pod was recreated twice tonight and the script rebuilt it in about a minute each time. A later role re-runs setup.sh and gets its own lane: the database name carries LEGION_ROLE. packages/contracts must be built (cd packages/contracts && bun run build) or e2e/agents.ts cannot import @legion/contracts.

The chromium project's own viewport is 1280x720, exactly READING_PANE_QUERY's width, so every browser row that drives the Inbox now runs with the pane on. That is 69 rows across 23 spec files, not the 8 the plan listed. e2e/inbox-pane.ts holds the shared helpers (hasReadingPane, inboxList, inboxPane, selectedRow, selectRow, askCard, askControls, listScrollTop, centreRow) every one of them now reads the Inbox through.

An approval's pane body is VersionView, never an AskCard, so at pane width the Inbox page draws no card for an approval request. Two approval rows that need a half-made answer on a card (approval.e2e.ts:354 and :404) were moved to the Inbox drawer, the one Inbox surface that passes pane={false} and so keeps today's card at every width.

deviations: The plan's departure 1 was rejected by the architect (dispatch://INFRA-575/comment/93a893db-8b1b-4614-a3f0-314f679a110b) and this change follows the ruling: the approval column renders the latest version with features/doc/VersionView.tsx and marks it with editor decorations, which packages/proof-editor now draws (setTextDecorations and setBlockWidgets on ProofEditorHandle). The plan was reissued as version 6 with task T5b for it.

The spec's R5 asks for removed and added words to be marked inside a changed block. On the rendered document the removed words have no characters to mark, so they are drawn as widget decorations at the offset the surviving text closed over — which is why BlockWidget carries an optional offset as well as a block index. The change view, which shows source text, marks them as a del as the spec says.

The plan's T6 named 8 existing spec files to update. The whole-project run found 23: the 8 plus agent-name, agents, approval, close-withdraws-asks, document, issue, keyboard-palette, live, nav, phone, references, refresh-freshness, threads and workspace. Every one is rewritten against the pane; none was narrowed to a width that hides it.
openQuestions: The pane holds the selected row against the server, not only against the reader's hand: `handId = paneShown ? selectedId : anchor?.id` (Inbox.tsx), so heldRow keeps a row Dispatch has withdrawn or resolved elsewhere listed until the reader selects another row, and an otherwise empty list can still show one. That is plan decision D3's own rule ('the selected row the server drops while the reader has not touched it stays in place … until the reader selects another row'), and the first row is selected the moment the Inbox opens, so the rule now applies to a row the reader never touched. Three browser rows read it (threads:450, close-withdraws-asks:212, approval:246) and were written against it. The architect owns whether a withdrawn question should instead leave at once.

ProofDocument in pane mode reports an admission refusal upward through onUnavailable rather than drawing the document page's repair or rebuild prompt, and the pane falls back to today's card with 'Open page'. The page's own behaviour is unchanged.
discoveredComplexity: No client-side markdown block splitter existed, so document-blocks.ts had to take over the fence rules decision-blocks.ts held privately (OPENING_FENCE, CODE_FENCE, BLANK_LINE, closingFenceAfter, codeFenceEnd) and serve both; cutDecisionBlocks' own suite and the contract fixtures under packages/contracts/fixtures/decision-blocks pass unchanged.

A document built by setMarkdown does carry a fresh blockId on every block, including an untyped paragraph, but those ids bear no relation to a baseline version's, so the decorations name a block by its index among the document's top-level children instead. A widget decoration survives the read-only editor's redraw: set, setMarkdown, drawn again.

Four defects of the new code were found only by the browser rows, not by any unit test: the Inbox re-created its list whenever the selection emptied (dropping keyboard focus mid-write), a snooze the pane head refused was never shown, ?item= kept naming a row the reader had just deferred, Enter was swallowed for a card's own buttons, and — found by the whole-project run — a click on a short row's owner link could not leave the Inbox. Each is fixed with a unit test that fails before the fix.
